title: Daybreak ops outline and rollback ladder — quicknotes
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact runbook for the Daybreak feature launch (target weekend window). It combines the short preflight checklist, a condensed 72-hour rollout calendar, the decision ladder for rollback/slowdown, and a draft release-notes blob we can refine for customer comms. Use this as the single source for the on-call and release conductor for the launch day.

Scope & constraints:
- Applies to hosted API + Dedicated pools in us-west1, eu-west1 (staggered regional rollout).
- Does NOT include Private on-prem bundles (separate package).
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms for text-generation baseline.
- Cost telemetry sampling enabled (1% tokens) during canary.

72h compact calendar (high-level):
- D-3 (Wed): Final smoke in staging, preflight checklist pass, docs snapshot, notify SRE and CS.
- D-2 (Thu): Canary image baked, load test at 10% of expected production QPS for 30m. Confirm autoscaler policy.
- D-1 (Fri): Dry-run cut: push to canary lane (internal only), run synthetic user journeys, validate KV cache warmup.
- D0 (Sat, 02:00–08:00 UTC): Regional micro-canary in us-west1 (1% traffic → 5% over 60m). If green, expand to 15% and keep for 2h.
- D0+1 (Sat afternoon): Expand to eu-west1 micro-canary (same pattern). Monitor for 8h then global ramp if no signals.
- D0+2 (Sun): Full ramp decision and customer-facing release notes published if metrics stable.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic shift):
- [ ] Canary build artifact present and pinned (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created and pinned: latency, error-rate, token-cost, model-fallback-rate.
- [ ] Smoke tests (auth, rate-limit, quota paths) passing in staging with identical config.
- [ ] KV cache evictions measured and within expected envelope for median sequence length.
- [ ] Rollback playbooks staged in runbook tooling and tested (simulated failures).
- [ ] CS & growth notified with embargoed release notes draft, support rotation scheduled.

Telemetry & alert thresholds (quick guide):
- Critical (immediate rollback): sustained >=3x baseline error-rate for 5m OR p95 latency >= 600ms for 5m.
- High (hold ramp / investigate): 1.5–3x error-rate OR p95 latency 200–600ms for 15m OR token-cost spike >40% over baseline.
- Medium (watch): small anomalies (10–50% deviance) in any single region for 30m.

Rollback ladder (decision steps):
1) Canary anomaly detected (high): pause expansion, revert to previous model variant in canary lane, notify stakeholders.
2) If error-rate persists post-variant swap: throttle traffic back to 10% and run targeted smoke tests for dependent subsystems.
3) If persisted >30 minutes and cross-region: initiate partial rollback (affected region) and open SEV-2 incident.
4) If global impact or customer-facing degradation: full rollback (return traffic routing to last known-good routing policy) and execute post-mortem template.

Communication plan (ops cadence):
- T-24h: Slack announcement in #release-ops and #sre-watch with runbook pointer.
- T-1h: Standby ping to on-call SRE, release conductor, and CS lead.
- During canary: 20m status updates pinned to release thread; immediate call if critical threshold hit.
- Post-release: Publish public-facing release notes (draft below), internal incident summary if any abnormalities.

Draft release notes (customer-facing, short):
- Title: Daybreak rollout — improved throughput and reduced tail latency
- Summary: We deployed a serving runtime update that improves throughput for long-context generation and reduces p95 latency for common workloads. No action required.
- Known limitations: Small percentage of sessions may see transient latency increases during the initial cache warmup window; we auto-fallback to previous model variant if errors occur.
- Contact: support@redwood.ai and your account engineer.

Quick TODOs (open items):
- [ ] Lock capacity reservations for Dedicated pools for D0–D+2 (Samir).
- [ ] Finalize change to autoscaler warmup policy (Evelyn).
- [ ] Add synthetic traffic pattern that simulates prefix-sharing workloads (Jordan).
- [ ] Run one additional 60m soak with the 1.5x median sequence length.

Notes to self / rough observations:
- Cache warmup seems sensitive to token distribution; we should instrument prefix reuse rate as a metric in future runs.
- Consider adding a short-circuit fallback that routes long-context requests to the "economy" variant if latency grows beyond threshold while keeping the short-context fast-path active.

Post-release checklist (within 24h):
- [ ] Confirm no customer-facing incidents and error-rate returned to baseline.
- [ ] Collect cost-sample reports and compare per-token unit economics.
- [ ] Schedule a 48h retrospective focused on telemetry gaps and rollout pacing.

If anything ambiguous during the launch, treat safety first: throttle, fall back, and escalate. Keep comms tight and small to avoid noisy signal.

End of quicknotes — merge into the canonical runbook and fill the TODOs before D-1.
